Your data 3D. So instead of A <- arrayspecs(data1, 8, 2), which is for eight landmarks with two coordinates apiece, you would use 
A <- arrayspecs(data1, 8, 3)

On Fri, Apr 28, 2023 at 4:35 PM Haley Amplo <haley...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,
I'm relatively new to R and the geomorph package, and have primarily been following the plethodon data tutorial and using "Quick Guide to Geomorph" to learn how to do the basic tasks. I've been able to successfully play with the plethodon$land data. I have also exported the plethodon$land data to an excel file so I could try and mimic the format for my own data.

However, even after manipulating my excel file to better match the pleth data and the way an array is formatted in the Quick Guide document, I'm still running into multiple issues. For starters, I can't seem to get my data to turn from 2D into 3D data using the arrayspecs() function [A <- arrayspecs(data1, 8, 2)]. I've tried setting p = 8 (number of landmarks), 24 (number of columns) and 96 (total number of data points outside of the header) and each time it still tells me that my matrix dimensions do not match my input. I've attached all the relevant files I've mentioned plus my R notebook. I'm really at a loss for what I'm doing wrong. I assume I'm not formatting my .csv file correctly, but I've tried changing the format multiple times as well and nothing has helped.

Best fishes and thanks in advance for any and all help!!
Hale Amplo
